alignments.note: Rule 58: the adjective and its expressed noun are both anarthrous, so the supplied determiner belongs to the noun and the adjective stands bare as *few*. Reading English *a few* as a fused quantifier and keeping *a* here is the competing analysis, on the model of rule 29's *a hundred*; rule 58 forbids reading a supplied determiner off the word order that puts it beside the adjective, and MRK.8.1 gives *a ... multitude* to the noun in the same shape.

Rule 58: the noun carries the supplied determiner, discontinuously around *few* under rule 15. Rule 66 keeps the head on *fishes*, which glosses the lexeme's root, *small* rendering the diminutive suffix.

review_notes: The competing reading is that English *a few* is a fused quantifier whose *a* is not the noun's determiner, on the model of rule 29's *a hundred*. It is named in the unit note. Rule 29 is scoped to a compound numeral idiom with the noun as a separate token, and rule 58's own reasoning - a determiner determines the noun phrase, an attributive adjective is only a modifier inside it - reaches a quantity adjective as readily as a quality one.

The head on ἰχθύδια stays *fishes* under rule 66: *fishes* glosses the lexeme's root and *small* renders the diminutive suffix, which is the same test 8.4 uses to head ἐρημίας on *desert* rather than on the generic *place*.
